Loren nació en <strong>San José de los A: Loren was born in San José de los Arroyos, in the heart of Paraguay. There, as in so many Paraguayan homes, cooking was passed down without books: by watching mothers and grandmothers knead chipa, curdle cheese and light the fire for the Sunday barbecue.
Esas recetas de sus padres y abuelos son: Those recipes from her parents and grandparents are still, to this day, the foundation of everything that leaves our kitchen.
«Nuestra intención es que al probar un b: "Our aim is that with one bite we can take our guests all the way to Paraguay."
Bandeja de empanadas, croquetas y chipas: Tray of homemade empanadas, croquettes and chipas
Con la ilusión de dar un futuro mejor a: Hoping to give her family a better future, Loren emigrated to Spain. At first she had to leave her children in Paraguay; she worked tirelessly and, in just one year, managed to bring them over.
Estudió cocina, trabajó en restaurantes: She studied cooking, worked in restaurants and learnt the trade from the inside, without ever losing the flavours of home.
Abrir en plena <em>pandemia</em>: Opening in the middle of a pandemic
Cuando el mundo cerraba, Loren abrió. Ju: While the world was closing, Loren opened. Together with her husband, José Manuel, she chose the name and set up Loren Gastrobar on Carrer de la Muntanya: a small place with 19 seats inside and 12 on the terrace, near Clot and Camp de l'Arpa metro stations.
La chipa guazú se convirtió en la bander: Chipa guazú became the flagship of the house, and empanadas, sopa paraguaya and mbejú started travelling all over Barcelona thanks to delivery.
«Cuesta, pero no me arrepiento.»: "It's hard, but I don't regret it."
El 28 de octubre de 2022 nació <strong>L: On 28 October 2022, Loren Restobar was born: more tables, a bigger menu and a slightly more refined offer, with new stars such as mandi'ó chyryry and the mixed grill served on a brazier.
Hoy toda la familia Loren te recibe bajo: Today the whole Loren family welcomes you under that name at Carrer de la Muntanya 115, with the same home cooking as ever and a terrace that's full every weekend.
El streamer Ibai Llanos organizó un «Mun: Streamer Ibai Llanos organised a "Food World Cup" decided by public vote, and the dish chosen to represent Paraguay was Loren's free-range chicken vorí vorí, which faced Uruguay's chivito in the round of 16.
Paraguay ganó en Instagram, la prensa pa: Paraguay won on Instagram, the Paraguayan press got behind it and thousands of compatriots voted from all over the world. The chivito went through, but the pride stayed at home.
«Perdimos esta vez, pero estamos prepara: "We lost this time, but we're ready to come back."
«Son 6 años de mucha ilusión y lucha con: "These have been 6 years of great hope and constant hard work to bring you the best of Paraguayan cuisine in Barcelona." That's how Loren celebrated with those who make this little corner possible: the Paraguayan community that finds a piece of home here and the locals who discover it every day.
«Cada paraguayo que pisa el local trae u: "Every Paraguayan who comes in brings a foreign friend."
Diez días de votación en Instagram, TikT: Ten days of voting on Instagram, TikTok and YouTube. Over 1.7 million votes in total. Paraguay won clearly on Instagram; Uruguay came out on top on TikTok and YouTube.
Para Loren fue mucho más que una votació: For Loren it was much more than a vote: "It was Paraguay united by its food."
Un negocio familiar de verdad: aquí te a: A true family business: the family serves you, they recommend dishes as if you were one of them and, if you like, they'll speak to you in Guaraní.
La guardiana de las recetas. Cocina cada: The keeper of the recipes. She cooks every day and won't let a dish out unless it tastes of Paraguay.
Compañero de Loren y de la aventura desd: Loren's partner in life and in this adventure from day one. Together they chose the name of the house.
Hijo de Loren, formado en administración: Loren's son, trained in restaurant management. Without him, she says, nothing would work the same.
Jennifer, Romina y todo el equipo de sal: Jennifer, Romina and the whole front-of-house team: the names that come up most in your reviews.
Somos lo que <em>te hacemos sentir</em>: We are what we make you feel
No es solo un eslogan. Es la forma en la: It's not just a slogan. It's how we cook, how we serve and how we open the door every morning at nine.
Recetas de familia, ingredientes de siem: Family recipes, traditional ingredients and Guaraní as the language of the house. Paraguay with no disguises.
Raciones generosas, trato cercano y una: Generous portions, a warm welcome and a table where nobody is a stranger. Pets are welcome too.
Guaranias de fondo, celebraciones, fútbo: Guarania music, celebrations, football and Paraguayan parties: people come here to enjoy themselves.
Los fines de semana, gran parte de nuest: At weekends, many of our tables fill up with Paraguayan families who come from all over Barcelona —and from other cities— for their vorí vorí, their pira caldo or the soyo with tortillita that reminds them of home.
Celebramos el <strong>Día de la Guarania: We celebrate Guarania Day with the classic songs, Guaraní Language Day with teacher Mbo'ehára Marce, who came to check whether we'd serve him in Guaraní (spoiler: we did), and every national holiday with our shirts on.
Y cuando alguien nos dice que la comida: And when someone tells us the food "tastes exactly like back home", we know we're on the right track.

Maíz, mandioca y queso. Con esos tres in: Corn, cassava and cheese. With those three ingredients, Guaraní wisdom and centuries of cultural blending, Paraguay created one of the tastiest —and least known— cuisines in South America. Here it is, dish by dish.

Si entiendes estos tres ingredientes, en: Understand these three ingredients and you understand Paraguay. They're in almost everything we cook, and many of our classics are made without wheat.
Tierno (choclo) o en harina. Es la base: Fresh (choclo) or as cornmeal. It's the base of chipa guazú, sopa paraguaya and the little balls in vorí vorí.
La yuca. Acompaña cada comida como aquí: Also called yuca. It goes with every meal like bread does here, and its starch gives us mbejú. Fried, boiled or sautéed.
Fresco, tierno, en cuajada. Da jugosidad: Fresh, soft, as curd. It makes sopa paraguaya juicy, melts in the mbejú and hides inside the vorí balls.
